title: Morning Brief — Mon 23 Nov

stories.board: Stocks bounce back after big AI selloff
stories.headline: Stock prices point up after a very bad week for AI companies
stories.what: Last week the S&P 500 fell 8.6 percent, its worst week in a long time, as AI and chip company stocks dropped. This morning futures (early bets on where prices go) are up strongly, led by Nvidia.
stories.why: Many people's savings and retirement money are tied to these big tech stocks.
stories.sides: No major disagreement: outlets on all sides report the drop and the bounce; worries include a reported SEC (US money watchdog) probe of Nvidia's accounting.

stories.board: Mexico catches top cartel boss El Chapo Isidro
stories.headline: Mexico's army captures one of the FBI's 10 most wanted
stories.what: Soldiers caught Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, a Sinaloa drug cartel (crime gang) leader, in a Friday night raid. Fighting followed in Sinaloa, and four soldiers were killed.
stories.why: His gang is accused of moving drugs into the US, and the US had offered up to 5 million dollars for him.
stories.sides: No major disagreement: Mexico and the US both say US intelligence (secret information) helped.

stories.board: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler for $44 billion
stories.headline: Two big cybersecurity companies plan to join together
stories.what: CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler for about 44 billion US dollars, paid in its own shares instead of cash. Both companies protect computers and networks from hackers.
stories.why: It would make one of the biggest cybersecurity (computer safety) companies in the world.
stories.sides: No major disagreement; regulators (government rule checkers) still have to approve it.

stories.board: Israel unity talks stuck; Eisenkot deadline Dec 6
stories.headline: Israel still has no new government after Netanyahu-Eisenkot talks
stories.what: Sunday's four-hour talks ended with no deal. Eisenkot has until Dec 6 (maybe Dec 20) to form a government, and says he may form an emergency (minority) government if talks fail.
stories.why: This decides who leads Israel next.
stories.sides: Each camp blames the other: they still split on Ben-Gvir, court laws and who is prime minister first.

quick_hits: Ontario set late-November heat records on Saturday; now lake-effect snow (snow made over warm lakes) hits snowbelts, with only flurries for Toronto.
Bahrain says an Iranian attack hit an industrial site and hurt two people; tankers (oil ships) were also hit near Hormuz.
Toronto Jewish security leaders say the community needs about 50 million dollars more for safety upgrades as threats rise.
big_picture: After a scary week, markets are catching their breath, while Israel's government talks are still stuck.
